questions.question: What is an array?
options: A collection of elements stored in a sequence
questions.explanation: An array stores multiple elements in a sequence.

questions.question: What is the index of the first element in most programming languages?
questions.explanation: Most common programming languages use zero-based indexing.

questions.question: What is the complexity of direct array access by index?
questions.explanation: An element can generally be accessed directly using its index.

questions.question: What does array traversal mean?
options: Visiting the elements of an array
questions.explanation: Traversal means visiting array elements.

questions.question: What is the typical complexity of traversing all elements?
questions.explanation: Every element must be visited, resulting in O(n).

questions.question: Which search checks elements one by one?
questions.explanation: Linear search checks elements sequentially.

questions.question: What is the worst-case complexity of linear search?
questions.explanation: Linear search may need to inspect every element.

questions.question: What requirement does binary search normally have?
options: The array must have exactly 10 elements
questions.explanation: Binary search relies on sorted data.

questions.question: What is the typical complexity of binary search?
questions.explanation: Binary search eliminates approximately half of the search space each step.

questions.question: What can happen when inserting into the middle of an array?
options: Elements may need to be shifted
questions.explanation: Elements after the insertion position may need to move.

questions.question: Which operation removes an element?
questions.explanation: Deletion removes an element.

questions.question: What does bubble sort repeatedly compare?
options: Only the first and last elements
questions.explanation: Bubble sort repeatedly compares adjacent elements.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of sorting?
questions.explanation: Sorting arranges elements according to a chosen ordering.

questions.question: Which approach can be used to find the maximum value?
options: Traverse the array while tracking the largest value
questions.explanation: A single traversal can track the maximum value.

questions.question: What is the complexity of finding the maximum through one traversal?
questions.explanation: Every element may need to be examined.

questions.question: Which structure can help detect duplicates efficiently?
questions.explanation: A set can track values that have already been encountered.

questions.question: What does O(n) generally mean?
options: Work grows approximately with input size
questions.explanation: O(n) describes linear growth relative to input size.

questions.question: Which algorithm is generally faster for searching a sorted large array?
questions.explanation: Binary search reduces the search space by half at each step.

questions.question: What does zero-based indexing mean?
questions.explanation: Zero-based indexing starts counting positions from 0.

questions.question: Which factor should influence the choice of an array algorithm?
questions.explanation: The input and required operation determine which algorithm is appropriate.
